title: Computationally Derived Cribriform Area Index from Prostate Cancer Hematoxylin and Eosin Images Is Associated with Biochemical Recurrence Following Radical Prostatectomy and Is Most Prognostic in Gleason Grade Group 2.
summary: A UNet-inspired deep-learning model segmented invasive cribriform carcinoma on prostate H&E slides, enabling a computed cribriform area index (CAI). In a four-site cohort, higher CAI was associated with biochemical recurrence among ICC-positive cases (adjusted HR 1.19 per doubling, p=0.018); discrimination was modest and the association was weak in the overall cohort.
ai_technology: A UNet-inspired deep-learning segmentation model was trained on 325 annotated image tiles from 36 patients and applied to tumor regions; CAI is the proportion of annotated tumor area classified as cribriform carcinoma.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Among 411 patients with ICC morphology, CAI had c-index 0.62; doubling CAI was independently associated with biochemical recurrence among 298 ICC-positive patients (HR 1.19, 95% CI 1.03–1.38, p=0.018). Overall-cohort discrimination was weak (c-index 0.54).
evidence.unknown: The segmentation model was applied to a multi-institutional validation cohort of 749 patients; the source reports site-level patterns and recurrence associations. The modest discrimination and retrospective association do not establish clinical utility.
